name: Kick
description: A kick: a sine that drops in pitch, with a click on the front. `punch` is how far and how hard it drops; `decay` is how long it rings.

name: Snare
description: A snare: a short triangle thump under a burst of band-passed noise. `snap` brings the noise up.

name: Hat
description: A hi-hat from high-passed, crushed noise. `open` lengthens it from a tick to a wash. The pitch of the note does not matter.

name: Bass
description: A round bass: a saw with a sine an octave down, through a low-pass that rings a little at `res`.

name: Pluck
description: A plucked string, bright as it starts and dulling as it dies away. `tone` is how bright the attack is; `decay` how long the note lasts.

name: Pad
description: A slow pad: three saws a hair apart in pitch, softened by a low-pass. `detune` widens them; `attack` and `release` set how it swells in and fades out.

name: Lead
description: A singing lead: a saw with a touch of vibrato, through a low-pass at `cutoff`.

name: Bell
description: A struck bell: two sines, one bending the phase of the other. `decay` is how long it rings.

name: Kick deep

source:

    noise_freq: noise_freq,

name: Lowpass
description: Remove high frequencies. Resonance shapes the filter around cutoff. `sweep_depth` (in octaves) moves the cutoff up and down at `sweep_rate`; at 0 it stays put.

name: Ladder lowpass
description: A warmer low-pass in the style of a transistor ladder: four soft stages, and `drive` pushes the sound into them. Resonance near 1 rings and sings at the cutoff. `sweep_depth` (in octaves) moves the cutoff at `sweep_rate`.

name: Highpass
description: Remove low frequencies. Resonance shapes the filter around cutoff. `sweep_depth` (in octaves) moves the cutoff up and down at `sweep_rate`.

name: Bandpass
description: Keep a band of frequencies around the cutoff. `sweep_depth` (in octaves) moves the band up and down at `sweep_rate`.

name: Band cut
description: Cut a narrow band of frequencies around the cutoff. `sweep_depth` (in octaves) moves the band up and down at `sweep_rate`.

name: Equalizer
description: Raise or cut the lows, a band in the middle, and the highs.

name: Echo
description: Echoes with independent left/right timing, feedback and a dry/wet blend.

name: Glitch
description: Glitches on the same sound, one after another: stutter repeats the last piece, rewind plays it backwards, slow winds the sound down like a stopping tape, and crush reduces its sample rate and bit depth. Each is switched on by its own control (automate them, or set them from a command column) and the sound passes through untouched while all are off. A `stutter_shrink` below 1 makes a held stutter roll faster, a `stutter_gate` below 1 makes the repeats staccato, and a `stutter_reverse` above 0 plays them backwards, a `stutter_shape` gives each a fade-out (above 0) or swell (below 0), `stutter_damp` darkens each repeat more than the last, `stutter_attack` and `stutter_bend` shape the envelope of each repeat (a slow attack, or an exponential pluck), and `stutter_accent` makes every second repeat quieter.
source:
/// Glitches on the same sound, one after another: stutter repeats the last piece, rewind plays it backwards,
/// slow winds the sound down like a stopping tape, and crush reduces its sample rate and bit depth. Each is
/// switched on by its own control (automate them, or set them from a command column) and the sound passes
/// through untouched while all are off. A `stutter_shrink` below 1 makes a held stutter roll faster, a `stutter_gate` below 1 makes the repeats staccato, and a `stutter_reverse` above 0 plays them backwards, a `stutter_shape` gives each a fade-out (above 0) or swell (below 0), `stutter_damp` darkens each repeat more than the last, `stutter_attack` and `stutter_bend` shape the envelope of each repeat (a slow attack, or an exponential pluck), and `stutter_accent` makes every second repeat quieter.
fx glitch(
  stutter: 0..1 = 0,
  stutter_length: 1ms..1sec = 125ms,
  stutter_pitch: -24..24 = 0,
  stutter_shrink: 0.5..1 = 1,
  stutter_gate: 0.05..1 = 1,
  stutter_reverse: 0..1 = 0,
  stutter_shape: -1..1 = 0,
  stutter_damp: 0..0.95 = 0,
  stutter_attack: 0..1 = 0,
  stutter_bend: 0..1 = 0,
  stutter_accent: 0..1 = 0,
  rewind: 0..1 = 0,
  rewind_length: 1ms..1sec = 250ms,
  slow: 0..1 = 0,
  slow_time: 10ms..1sec = 400ms,
  crush: 0..1 = 0,
  crush_bits: 2..16 = 5,
  crush_rate: 200hz..20000hz = 4000hz,
  mix: 0..1 = 1
) {
  glitched = in
    .repeat_last(hold: stutter, length: stutter_length, pitch: stutter_pitch, shrink: stutter_shrink,
      gate: stutter_gate, reverse: stutter_reverse,
      shape: stutter_shape, damp: stutter_damp,
      attack: stutter_attack, bend: stutter_bend, accent: stutter_accent)
    .rewind_last(hold: rewind, length: rewind_length)
    .slow_down(hold: slow, time: slow_time)
    .apply(fn(s) { s.bitcrush(rate: crush_rate, bits: crush_bits) }, when: crush)
  out = in.crossfade(glitched, mix)
}

name: Room reverb
description: A room or hall: `room` is its size, `damp` how quickly the highs die away in it.

name: Ensemble
description: Gently widen the signal with a modulated delay chorus.

name: Swirl
description: A sweeping phaser: notches that move around `center`, fed back on themselves.

name: Tremolo
description: Amplitude tremolo. shape selects the LFO: 0 sine, 1 triangle, 2 square, 3 saw.

name: Compressor
description: Turn loud parts down: above the threshold the level is reduced by the ratio, and makeup brings the whole signal back up. `knee` rounds the corner at the threshold. `link` is how much the channels of a stereo sound share one squeeze: at 1 the loudest decides for both, so the image stays put; at 0 each side is squeezed on its own.

name: Overdrive
description: Warm or hard distortion. `drive` is how hard the signal is pushed, `tone` how bright it is. It runs at twice the sample rate, so bright sounds pushed hard don't fold harmonics back down as noise.

name: Lofi
description: Lo-fi: fewer bits and a lower sample rate, for grit.

name: Soft clip
description: Round off peaks that would clip, with no delay. `drive` is how hard the signal is pushed into the curve; the output is scaled so a full-scale input still reaches full scale. For a hard ceiling on the whole mix, the master has a lookahead limiter of its own.
